jobs.excerpt: As a Promo Team Lead, you will manage a team of promo writers, sound engineers, video editors, and dubbing partners to create high-quality promotional ads for Pocket FM audio series.
jobs.description:
As a Promo Team Lead, you will manage a team of promo writers, sound engineers, video editors, and dubbing partners to create high-quality promotional ads for Pocket FM audio series.

The role requires strong understanding of promo creation, ad storytelling, localization, dubbing workflows, quality control, team management, and creative optimization. You will oversee fresh promo creation, adaptation of ads from other geographies into Spanish, production quality, timely delivery, and reworks for ads that are not meeting performance benchmarks.

Key Responsibilities

    1. Team Leadership & Creative Direction

  • Lead and guide promo writers, sound engineers, video editors, and external dubbing partners.

  • Provide creative direction across writing, dubbing, audio mixing, video editing, and final delivery.

  • Ensure the team is well-utilized, motivated, and aligned with business and creative goals.

  • Build a high-ownership culture focused on quality, speed, and performance.

    • 2. Promo Creation & Localization

  • Oversee the creation of fresh promo ads, trailers, and long-form promotional scripts for audio series.

  • Adapt successful ads from other geographies into Spanish Portuguese.

  • Ensure all promos are culturally relevant, emotionally engaging, and suitable for Spanish audiences.

  • Guide the team on hooks, story setup, emotional beats, cliffhangers, and audience entry points.

    • 3. Production & Quality Control

  • Own the end-to-end promo production process from brief to final asset delivery.

  • Quality check every stage, including writing, dubbing, audio mixing, video creation, and final output.

  • Review scripts, VO/dubbing output, audio edits, video cuts, captions, and final creatives.

  • Ensure every asset meets Pocket FM’s creative, language, production, and performance standards.

    • 4. Dubbing Agency Management

  • Identify, evaluate, and onboard dubbing agencies for Spanish Portuguese production.

  • Coordinate with agencies for script handover, voice casting, recording, revisions, and delivery.

  • Review dubbing output for pronunciation, emotion, pacing, tone, and character fit.

  • Track agency timelines, pending deliverables, feedback loops, and final submissions.

    • 5. Performance Reworks & Optimization

  • Review ads that are not meeting benchmark metrics and identify key creative issues.

  • Create detailed and actionable rework hypotheses to improve ad performance.

  • Suggest improvements such as stronger hooks, sharper conflicts, better pacing, improved localization, or revised visuals.

  • Guide the team in creating alternate openings, new versions, and stronger creative angles.

  • Apply campaign learnings to improve future promo concepts and execution.

    • 6. Process, Tracking & Reporting

  • Maintain show-level trackers for all ads being written, adapted, dubbed, edited, reviewed, and delivered.

  • Track ownership, status, timelines, delays, feedback, and final delivery for each asset.

  • Share weekly progress reports with the India team and relevant stakeholders.

  • Create SOPs, checklists, and workflows to avoid leakages across the production process.

    • 7. AI Tool Adoption

  • Use GenAI tools for ad writing, ideation, VO production, image creation, video creation, and workflow improvement.

  • Guide the team in using AI tools to improve speed, quality, and efficiency.

  • Continuously explore new AI tools and workflows for promo production.

  • Ensure AI-assisted outputs are reviewed for storytelling quality, cultural accuracy, and production readiness.

    • 8. Market & Audience Understanding

  • Apply strong understanding of Spanish consumer behavior, content consumption habits, and market trends.

  • Ensure promos feel native, relevant, and compelling for Spanish audiences.

  • Stay updated on digital ads, audio entertainment, trailer formats, and performance creative trends.

Qualifications

  • Degree in Filmmaking, Marketing, Advertising, Media, Communications, or a related field.

  • 8+ years of experience in ad creation, promo creation, trailer development, marketing creatives, ad copywriting, or performance creative production.

  • Strong understanding of marketing, ad storytelling, promo creation, and audience engagement.

  • Experience leading creative or production teams, including writers, editors, sound engineers, or external vendors.

  • Excellent command of English and Spanish.

  • Strong understanding of Spanish consumer behavior, content consumption patterns, and cultural nuances.

  • Experience working with dubbing agencies, VO artists, production teams, or post-production vendors.

  • Skilled in GenAI tools for writing, VO production, image creation, video creation, and creative workflow improvement.

  • Ability to create SOPs, trackers, review systems, and scalable creative processes.

  • Strong analytical ability to review ad performance and convert insights into actionable creative reworks.

  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and leadership skills.

  • Strategic thinker with strong ownership and business growth orientation.

  • Understanding of performance marketing on Meta and UAC is a plus.

The ideal candidate is a creative leader who understands storytelling, promo production, and performance-driven advertising. They should be able to lead a multi-functional team, manage dubbing partners, maintain strong quality control, and deliver high-quality promo assets at scale.

They should have strong knowledge of Spanish audiences, excellent creative judgment, hands-on production understanding, and the ability to turn performance feedback into clear creative action.

jobs.excerpt: About Prilenia Prilenia Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on the urgent mission of developing novel therapeutics to slow the progression of neurodegenerative diseases and neurodevelopmental disorders, is looking for a Director/Senior Director, GCP Quality Assurance Lead, to support programs in both Huntington’s Disease and ALS.
jobs.description:
About Prilenia

Prilenia Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on the urgent mission of developing novel therapeutics to slow the progression of neurodegenerative diseases and neurodevelopmental disorders, is looking for a Director/Senior Director, GCP Quality Assurance Lead, to support programs in both Huntington’s Disease and ALS.

We are a flexible, fast-moving team that is quickly advancing a potential therapy poised to have major impact on the lives of patients and their families. Our lead product candidate, pridopidine, holds Orphan Drug Designation in both Huntington’s disease (HD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in the U.S. and EU, as well as Fast Track designation from the FDA for the treatment of HD. Prilenia is conducting global Phase 3 clinical trials in both HD and ALS.

​Pridopidine has the potential to be a pivotal treatment to address HD and ALS disease progression. Prilenia believes pridopidine’s novel mechanism of action as a Sigma-1 receptor agonist also gives it potential in numerous other neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental conditions.

To learn more about our story and company culture, visit us at

About the role

The Director/Sr. Dir, GCP Quality Assurance is Prilenia's primary quality lead for clinical development, owning GCP quality end-to-end from study start-up through inspection readiness, and serving as sponsor QA counterpart to our CRO(s) and Ferrer's QA team. The role also provides proportionate QA oversight for pharmacovigilance (GVP) and pre-clinical (GLP) activities.

The ideal candidate is both a hands-on quality practitioner and a strategic partner to Clinical Development, Regulatory Affairs, Drug Safety, and Biostatistics, combining deep GCP/GvP/GLP expertise with the executive presence to influence cross-functional teams and senior leadership.

Roles and Responsibilities:

    GCP Quality - Core Focus

    • Ensure all Prilenia-sponsored trials are conducted, documented, and reported in compliance with applicable regulations, ICH guidelines, and Prilenia's SOPs.
    • Serve as Prilenia's day-to-day QA lead for Phase 3 clinical operations, embedded in the program team from protocol review through clinical study report sign-off.
    • Act as sponsor QA counterpart to CRO QA teams and to Ferrer's QA function, maintain quality oversight of outsourced trial execution, align on standards, and manage issue escalation.
    • Oversee eTMF quality, manage protocol deviations and GxP non-conformances, drive CAPA resolution with CROs and sites, and maintain continuous inspection readiness.
    • Lead inspection readiness and management for regulatory authority inspections (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA); serve as primary QA contact, coordinate responses to observations, and oversee regulatory commitment closure.
    • Author and maintain GCP and related SOPs; define and track quality metrics and KPIs for senior leadership.
    • Oversee clinical site, CRO, and vendor audits; review reports, manage CAPA resolution; review and approve Quality Agreements.

      • QA Partnership & SME for GLP and GVP

      • Serve as GVP QA partner and SME to Drug Safety: oversee PV systems, vendor quality performance, and vendor audits; support CAPA resolution for safety findings; ensure compliance with EU GvP modules, FDA 21 CFR Part 312, and ICH E2 series.
      • Serve as GLP QA partner and SME for externally conducted pre-clinical studies; ensure compliance with OECD Principles of GLP and applicable national regulations.

        • QMS & Cross-Functional Leadership

        • Contribute to Prilenia's fit-for-purpose QMS, SOP lifecycle, quality event tracking, training, and regulatory intelligence.
        • Represent QA on clinical program teams and relevant governance forums.
        • Champion a proactive quality and compliance culture, making quality an enabler of clinical program success rather than a compliance exercise.
        • Mentor junior QA staff and foster professional development within the quality function.

Qualifications:

    Required

    • Bachelor’s degree or higher in life sciences, pharmacy, or a related discipline; advanced degree (MSc, PharmD) preferred.
    • Minimum 10 years of GCP QA experience within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or CRO industry, with at least 3 years in a leadership or director-level role at a biotech company.
    • Demonstrated expertise across GCP, GvP, and GLP quality frameworks; hands-on experience conducting and managing audits in all three domains.
    • Deep knowledge of ICH E6(R2/R3), ICH E2 series, FDA 21 CFR Parts 11/50/54/56/312, EU Clinical Trials Regulation (No. 536/2014), EU GvP modules, and OECD Principles of GLP.
    • Proven experience leading or managing regulatory authority inspections (FDA, EMA, MHRA, or equivalent) to successful outcomes.
    • Experience building or significantly maturing a QMS in a small-to-mid-size pharmaceutical setting.
    • Proficiency with eTMF systems (e.g., Veeva Vault, Wingspan) and electronic QMS platforms.
    • Exceptional communication skills; able to translate complex regulatory requirements into clear guidance for diverse audiences.
    • Highly autonomous, proactive, and resilient; comfortable in a fast-paced, resource-efficient environment.

      • Desirable

We are looking for a Part-Time Shopify Developer to join the team and take ownership of the technical and development side of the Shopify stores.

You will work alongside a full-time Shopify Manager who will handle the day-to-day site operations, catalogue management and content updates. Your focus will be on development, troubleshooting, integrations and ongoing technical improvements.

You will primarily be working within the existing environment — modifying, extending, troubleshooting and maintaining what is already there, as well as handling general Shopify theme and Liquid development.

Key Responsibilities

  • Modify, extend and troubleshoot existing Shopify apps and integrations, including the custom product recommendation engine.

Must-Have Skills & Experience

  • Strong hands-on experience with Shopify Plus development.

  • Familiarity with Matrixify or similar bulk import/export tools.
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal day-to-day supervision.

Nice-to-Have Experience

jobs.excerpt: ABOUT GREYSTAR Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing.
jobs.description:
ABOUT GREYSTAR


Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. Headquartered in Charleston, South Carolina, Greystar manages and operates over $350 billion of real estate in more than 260 markets globally with offices throughout North America, Europe, South America, and the Asia-Pacific region. Greystar is the largest operator of apartments in the United States, managing over one million units/beds globally. Across its platforms, Greystar has nearly $79 billion of assets under management, including over $34 billion of development assets and over $36.5 billion of regulatory assets under management. Greystar was founded by Bob Faith in 1993 to become a provider of world-class service in the rental residential real estate business. To learn more, visit .

JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

Reporting to the Senior Director of Employee Relations, the Regional Employee Relations Director (West) leads a team of ER Directors across 14 states spanning the West and Midwest, and serves as the regional authority on employee relations strategy, compliance, investigations, and people risk management.

The West Region is one of Greystar’s most complex operating environments. California alone represents a dense portfolio spanning multiple lines of business, each operating under one of the most demanding regulatory and employment law frameworks in the country. The broader 14-state footprint adds significant geographic and jurisdictional breadth. Together, the West Region’s unique structure requires an ER regional leader who is as fluent in California labor law as they are in leading a team and supporting a sizable employee and senior leadership portfolio — someone who can operate proactively, build manager capability across a geographically dispersed business, and serve as a trusted strategic partner to senior leaders navigating real and daily people risk.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Lead and Develop the West Region ER Team

  • Direct, coach, and develop a team of ER Directors embedded across the region, building bench strength and ensuring consistent, high-quality ER support to business leaders.
  • Establish and maintain clear team norms, case management standards, and quality calibration practices across the region.
  • Identify developmental opportunities for team members and actively sponsor their growth within the ER function.

Navigate Regulatory and Compliance Complexity

  • Serve as the subject-matter authority on California employment law — including wage and hour compliance, PAGA potential exposure and cure strategies, worker classification framework, Cal/OSHA obligations, and California’s expanding pay transparency requirements.
  • Stay ahead of the legislative calendar across the portfolio, translating emerging obligations into proactive regional practice.
  • Lead the regional response to regulatory inquiries, agency charges, and government audits in partnership with senior business and People & Culture leaders, Legal, and internal process and system SMEs.

Manage Complex Employee Relations Matters and Investigations

  • Personally manage and oversee the team’s handling of the region’s highest-complexity ER matters and cases.
  • Work closely with business leaders, Regional Director peers, and the Senior Director to resolve complicated ER issues, team member complaints, and a broad range of HR generalist initiatives.

Be a Trusted Strategic Partner to the Business

  • Serve as a strategic consultant and executive coach to West Region business leaders, enhancing manager capability and decision-making quality on people matters.
  • Provide strategic guidance on HR activities to mitigate risk and optimize resources, translating ER data and trends into actionable insights for regional leadership.
  • Ensure that employment practices across the West Region comply with Greystar’s policies and guide ER activities to help leaders, managers, and team members resolve issues effectively.
  • Participate in executing Company strategies, initiatives, and programs that build and sustain a high-performance culture.

Drive Training, Data, and Continuous Improvement

  • Work with the business to highlight key trends in employee relations case law across the region and actively drive training, systems, and process improvement in response.
  • Design and deliver manager education on the region’s most complex compliance and ER topics, equipping leaders with the knowledge and tools to make sound, well-informed people decisions.
  • Provide rigorous data analysis and reporting on ER trends, case outcomes, and compliance metrics to inform business decisions and Senior Director reporting.
  • Integrate and partner with fellow Regional Directors, the ER team, Legal, and the Senior Director to implement consistent, best-in-class ER solutions.

Requirements

Experience & Expertise

  • 10+ years of progressively responsible Human Resources experience, culminating in a Director or Regional Director-level ER role; substantial, years-long multi-unit, field-based, and multi-state experience is essential, with significant California-specific experience required.
  • Deep, practiced fluency in California employment law is required — not just familiarity with it.
  • Significant hands-on experience directly managing complex, multi-state employee relations issues from beginning/in-take to conclusion, manager and leadership coaching, and implementation of outcomes.
  • Demonstrated experience leading and developing a team of HR or ER professionals across a distributed geography; experience leading a remote team is an enormous plus.
  • Experience using HR and ER metrics for strategic action-planning and executive-level reporting.
  • Experience with Workday and Dayforce a plus.

Leadership & Interpersonal Strengths

  • Self-motivated and comfortable with ambiguity; does not require positional authority to drive outcomes in a fast-paced, high-performance environment.
  • Capable of building trust and credibility quickly with senior business leaders, employees, and legal counsel alike.
  • Excellent judgment — knows what they don’t know, asks the right questions, and reaches well-informed decisions that minimize organizational risk.
  • Compassionate leader who sustains collegiality, collaboration, and team orientation; able to influence change and build consensus across functions and levels.
  • Absolute and unquestioned integrity and confidentiality in all circumstances.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communicator; able to articulate complex legal or HR matters clearly for diverse audiences.
  • Multi-lingual a plus.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office suite; strong Excel and PowerPoint skills for data analysis and reporting.

Education

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field required.
  • Master’s Degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field a plus.
  • California HR certification preferred (e.g., SHRM-CP/SCP with California focus, PHR/SPHR, or equivalent state-specific credential).

The salary range for this position is $160,000 - $180,000 USD Annually.


Additional Compensation:


Many factors go into determining employee pay within the posted range including business requirements, prior experience, current skills and geographical location.

  • Corporate Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in a quarterly or annual bonus program based on individual and company performance.
  • Onsite Property Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in weekly, monthly, and/or quarterly bonus programs.

Robust Benefits Offered*:

  • Competitive Medical, Dental, Vision, and Disability & Life insurance benefits. Low (free basic) employee Medical costs for employee-only coverage; costs discounted after 3 and 5 years of service.
  • Generous Paid Time off. All new hires start with 15 days of vacation, 4 personal days, 10 sick days, and 11 paid holidays. Plus your birthday off after 1 year of service! Additional vacation accrued with tenure.
  • For onsite team members, onsite housing discount at Greystar-managed communities are available subject to discount and unit availability.
  • 6-Week Paid Sabbatical after 10 years of service (and every 5 years thereafter).
  • 401(k) with Company Match up to 6% of pay after 6 months of service.
  • Paid Parental Leave and lifetime Fertility Benefit reimbursement up to $10,000 (includes adoption or surrogacy).
  • Employee Assistance Program.
  • Critical Illness, Accident, Hospital Indemnity, Pet Insurance and Legal Plans.
  • Charitable giving program and benefits.

*Benefits offered for full-time employees. For Union and Prevailing Wage roles, compensation and benefits may vary from the listed information above due to Collective Bargaining Agreements and/or local governing authority.


Greystar will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.


Greystar is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.


This position may be performed remotely anywhere within the United States except the state of Alaska.

Greystar does not conduct any interviews via text or messaging, and all communication will come from official Greystar email addresses (@greystar.com). May Mobility is entering an exciting phase of growth as we expand our first-of-its-kind autonomous shuttle and mobility services across the nation. Launched in 2017 with a strong team of experienced roboticists and software engineers with decades of experience fielding robotic systems in the wild, May Mobility is looking to expand its team of robotics engineers with a background in robotics or autonomous vehicles.

As Perception Lead, you will own the technical direction of how our vehicles see and interpret the world. This is a hands-on role focused on three priorities: advancing scene detection so the system reliably recognizes its operating context and engages the right behavior; hardening perception against sensor degradation and adverse weather (rain, snow, fog, glare, low light, and sensor soiling or occlusion) so performance degrades gracefully and safely; and driving major architectural updates to evolve our perception stack into a scalable, maintainable, production-grade foundation. This role is about creating data-related content fordisplay on social channels. If you have the skill to work with raw data and you love to turn data into compelling visuals that create scroll-stopping experiences on social channels, this may be for you!

What you'll do

  • Create compelling content for social media channels
  • Analyze Qwoted's platform data (pitch activity, source requests, response rates, demographic patterns, beat trends, etc.) to find angles worth telling
  • Build clean charts and graphics that are social media ready
  • Write short, punchy captions and summaries that explain the "so what" in plain English, built for social feeds first
  • Package findings with enough supporting data and context that a journalist could plausibly write a full story off of it (stats, methodology notes, a quote-ready line or two, sources)
  • Suggest new angles as you spend time in the data. We don't want someone who just executes a list, we want someone who spots things we haven't asked about yet

What you bring

  • A knack for finding the interesting thread in a boring dataset
  • Experience creating data visualization to get earned media pickup, not just internal reporting
  • A sense of how to translate graphs and data for social carousels (or videos) on social platforms
  • Ability to create interactive visuals
  • Newsroom or journalism background is a bonus
  • East Coast hours or general US-based availability preferred for overlap with our team

Technical Skills

  • Working knowledge of data analysis tools (SQL, R, Python) and visualization platforms (Observable, Flourish, etc.)
  • Experience with design and motion graphics tools (Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, Premiere, After Effects; also Canva or Affinity), plus data visualization/mapping tools (Mapcreator, Flourish, Infogram, Esri, Observable)
  • Familiarity with front-end frameworks/libraries such as Svelte, D3.js, and Three.js for building and organizing interactive projects

jobs.title: Program Manager, Solution Innovation
jobs.excerpt: Our team members are at the heart of everything we do.
jobs.description:
Our team members are at the heart of everything we do. At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today!

Job Details

The Program Manager, Solution Innovation is responsible for managing the solution innovation workstreams, governance process, and operating pathway that moves ideas, concepts, pilots, and solution opportunities through disciplined evaluation, prioritization, stage-gate review, roadmap alignment, and execution tracking. Reporting to the Group Product Owner – Solution Innovation and Design, this role ensures the solution innovation pathway is clearly documented, consistently applied, transparent to stakeholders, and aligned with CPS product and solution development priorities.

This role supports product strategy execution by translating innovation priorities, market insights, customer needs, and leadership decisions into structured program plans, committee routines, stage-gate deliverables, roadmap updates, and implementation requirements. The role maintains the operating infrastructure that enables the Group Product Owner, Product Development Committee, solution teams, commercialization partners, analytics, legal/compliance, operations, and other stakeholders to evaluate and advance innovation opportunities in a repeatable and measurable way.

This role does not own product strategy or final product prioritization decisions; instead, it owns the program management discipline, governance administration, process documentation, stakeholder coordination, dependency tracking, and reporting routines required to support timely and effective solution innovation decisions. The Program Manager ensures innovation items are organized, stage-gate materials are complete, committee decisions are captured, roadmap and backlog data are maintained, and risks, issues, decisions, and follow-ups are visible and actionable.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities:

Solution Innovation Pathway Management

  • Implement, maintain, and continuously improve the Solution Innovation pathway from idea intake through discovery, validation, pilot/proof-of-concept, scale recommendation, roadmap transition, and post-decision follow-up.

  • Translate the priorities of the Group Product Owner – Solution Innovation and Design into structured program plans, operating routines, meeting cadences, decision checkpoints, documentation requirements, and stakeholder deliverables.

  • Define and maintain pathway documentation including process maps, stage-gate expectations, intake criteria, readiness checklists, decision rights, artifacts, intake forms, governance calendars, and communication protocols.

  • Ensure the innovation pathway is applied consistently across solution workstreams while remaining flexible enough to support different types of innovation opportunities, pilots, prototypes, and business cases.

  • Identify process bottlenecks, ambiguous handoffs, inconsistent documentation, and decision delays; recommend and implement improvements to increase clarity, speed, accountability, and stakeholder alignment.

Product Development Committee Operations and Governance

  • Coordinate and manage the Product Development Committee operating rhythm, including agenda planning, materials intake, pre-read preparation, meeting facilitation support, decision documentation, action tracking, and follow-up communication.

  • Support the Group Product Owner in preparing innovation concepts, backlog recommendations, stage-gate materials, and roadmap updates for Product Development Committee review.

  • Ensure committee decisions, open questions, risks, approvals, deferrals, and next steps are captured accurately and communicated to appropriate stakeholders.

  • Maintain governance records and decision logs to support transparency, traceability, and accountability across innovation pathway decisions.

  • Monitor adherence to Product Development Committee processes and recommend refinements to governance structure, meeting cadence, decision standards, and escalation pathways.

Innovation Backlog and Roadmap Administration

  • Maintain the innovation backlog with current information on opportunity status, owner, strategic theme, stage-gate status, customer value, business rationale, dependencies, risks, target timing, and next actions.

  • Support roadmap administration for solution innovation initiatives by tracking milestones, sequencing, stage transitions, prioritization inputs, and linkage to CPS solution strategy.

  • Partner with the Group Product Owner and product stakeholders to ensure innovation backlog and roadmap data reflect current priorities, leadership decisions, capacity constraints, and dependencies.

  • Develop and maintain reporting views that allow leadership to understand backlog health, pathway throughput, stage-gate progress, pipeline constraints, and upcoming decisions.

  • Identify stale, duplicative, misaligned, or blocked backlog items and coordinate with owners to recommend disposition, refresh, escalation, or removal.

Stage-Gate Process Execution and Artifact Management

  • Manage stage-gate execution across solution innovation workstreams, including intake readiness, discovery documentation, problem statements, VOC summaries, pilot objectives, success criteria, feasibility inputs, risk assessments, and transition recommendations.

  • Ensure required artifacts are developed, updated, reviewed, and stored in the appropriate location before stage-gate reviews and committee discussions.

  • Coordinate with Product Owners, Product Managers, solution development teams, analytics, operations, commercialization, legal/compliance, finance, and other stakeholders to gather required stage-gate inputs.

  • Track gate decisions and follow-up actions, ensuring workstream owners understand expectations required to progress to the next stage.

  • Continuously evaluate whether stage-gate criteria and artifacts are fit for purpose and recommend changes that improve decision quality, speed, and consistency.

Innovation Workstream Program Management

  • Manage multiple solution innovation workstreams by developing and tracking workplans, milestones, deliverables, dependencies, risks, issues, communications, and stakeholder commitments.

  • Support cross-functional teams in defining scope, timelines, deliverables, resource needs, sequencing, decision points, and escalation paths for innovation initiatives.

  • Coordinate workstream planning and execution across Product, Solution Development, Commercialization, Enablement, Analytics, Operations, Legal/Compliance, Finance, and customer-facing functions.

  • Develop clear status updates and program views that communicate progress, blockers, decisions needed, upcoming milestones, and risks to the Group Product Owner and relevant stakeholders.

  • Proactively anticipate risks, dependency conflicts, resource constraints, and scope creep; present mitigation options and escalation recommendations to leadership.

Requirements, Business Case, and Product Lifecycle Support

  • Support development of product and solution requirements, enhancement plans, business cases, and lifecycle recommendations by coordinating inputs from product, strategy, analytics, customers, and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Help translate innovation strategy, market insights, customer needs, and committee decisions into actionable product plans, implementation requirements, stage-gate deliverables, and roadmap updates.

  • Coordinate operating cost, ROI, risk, readiness, adoption, and performance inputs needed to support innovation prioritization and product lifecycle decisions.

  • Support transition of validated innovation concepts into product roadmaps, commercialization planning, operational readiness, enablement planning, or scale recommendations as appropriate.

  • Ensure service expectations, operational readiness requirements, customer support implications, and risk considerations are documented for innovation opportunities moving toward pilot or launch.

Stakeholder Communication and Executive Reporting

  • Develop and maintaintimely, accurate, and concise reporting on innovation pipeline status, Product Development Committee decisions, stage-gate progress, roadmap updates, risks, issues, and action items.

  • Facilitate stakeholder discussions to build alignment on innovation priorities, process expectations, implementation approaches, dependencies, and next steps.

  • Prepare materials, dashboards, status reports, decision summaries, and executive updates for the Group Product Owner, Product Development Committee, CPS leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Use appropriate communication tools and formats to keep stakeholders informed and aligned across complex and interconnected innovation workstreams.

  • Translate complex process, product, and dependency information into clear summaries for both technical and non-technical audiences.

Continuous Improvement, SOPs, and Process Discipline

  • Develop, maintain, and improve standard operating procedures, templates, process documents, governance tools, communication practices, and stage-gate artifacts supporting the Solution Innovation pathway.

  • Conduct periodic process reviews and lessons-learned sessions to identify successful and unsuccessful pathway elements and apply improvements to future workstreams.

  • Identify opportunities for efficiency, process improvement, documentation quality, tool optimization, governance simplification, and improved stakeholder experience.

  • Implement repeatable program management practices that improve visibility, accountability, decision quality, data integrity, and workflow speed across solution innovation activities.

  • Promote consistent use of program management and product management tools, ensuring information is complete, current, and usable for decision-making.

Risk, Issue, Dependency, and Resource Tracking

  • Maintain risk, issue, dependency, and decision logs for solution innovation workstreams and governance processes.

  • Partner with stakeholders to identify mitigation plans, escalation needs, and alternative approaches when timelines, resources, scope, or dependencies are at risk.

  • Track resource needs, capacity constraints, and cross-functional dependencies that impact workstream progression or stage-gate readiness.

  • Use judgment and discretion in escalating issues to the Group Product Owner and relevant leadership when innovation progress, stakeholder commitments, or decision timing are at risk.

  • Ensureinnovation workstream risks and dependencies are visible in roadmap, backlog, and committee reporting.

Compliance and Other

  • Ensure solution innovation governance, documentation, and workstream processes comply with applicable company policies, privacy/security expectations, legal/compliance standards, and documentation requirements.

  • Perform related duties as assigned.

Experience and Educational Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree required in business administration, marketing, product management, project/program management, healthcare administration, information systems, engineering, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.

  • 6+ years of experience in product management, product strategy, program management, project management, business operations, innovation operations, or a related field required.

  • Experience managing cross-functional workstreams, governance processes, stage-gate models, product roadmaps, innovation pipelines, or product lifecycle processes preferred.

  • Experience supporting senior stakeholders, committees, governance forums, and executive reporting preferred.

  • Experience in healthcare, pharmacy services, technology-enabled services, product development, or portfolio/program management preferred.

  • Certification in agile, scrum, product management, project management, or program management preferred.

Minimum Skills, Knowledge, and Ability Requirements

  • Strong program and project management skills, including scope, schedule, milestone, dependency, risk, issue, and communication management.

  • Ability to manage multiple related workstreams directed toward common strategic objectives while maintaining reliable reporting and stakeholder alignment.

  • Strong understanding of product management concepts, including product strategy, roadmaps, requirements, business cases, lifecycle planning, go-to-market readiness, value metrics, and operational readiness.

  • Ability to facilitate stakeholder discussions, build alignment across competing priorities, and translate decisions into action plans and implementation requirements.

  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to maintain accurate documentation, decision logs, process artifacts, and governance records.

  • Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing with technical and non-technical audiences, senior stakeholders, cross-functional teams, and business partners.

  • Strong analytical, conceptual, and problem-solving skills with ability to evaluate program risks, process gaps, dependencies, and potential solutions.

  • Ability to create clear executive summaries, roadmap views, committee materials, status reports, dashboards, process documentation, and presentations.

  • Ability to use collaboration, product management, and program management tools to track work, communicate status, manage documentation, and maintain stakeholder visibility.

  • Ability to work independently, exercise judgment, manage ambiguity, prioritize effectively, and escalate issues appropriately.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Outlook, and related project / program management or collaboration tools such as Jira, Confluence, Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Planner, or similar platforms preferred.

What Cencora offers

We provide compensation, benefits, and resources that enable a highly inclusive culture and support our team members’ ability to live with purpose every day. In addition to traditional offerings like medical, dental, and vision care, we also provide a comprehensive suite of benefits that focus on the physical, emotional, financial, and social aspects of wellness. jobs.title: Senior Pricing Manager
jobs.excerpt: Redox is on a mission to accelerate healthcare’s transformation with useful data.
jobs.description:
Redox is on a mission to accelerate healthcare’s transformation with useful data. Redox Engine, a flexible interoperability platform, connects and powers real-time healthcare data exchange. With just one connection, data can be orchestrated across a growing network of 12,000+ systems and organizations, including 100+ electronic health record systems (EHRs). Redox processes over 1.2 billion messages per month across our health tech vendor, provider, payer, EHR, and life sciences customers.

Opportunity & Impact

As Director of Pricing, you will own how pricing works operationally at Redox. Pricing and packaging strategy is set by Product; your job is to take that strategy and make it real — turning it into deal-level guardrails, tools, and decisions that Sales can use every day. You will run Redox's Deal Desk for bespoke, non-standard deals: working directly with reps and reviewing Gong call recordings to understand what a customer needs, and structuring the right combination of platform fee, connection pricing, and transaction pricing for that specific deal.

You will also be the connective tissue between the field and Product: surfacing what's actually happening in negotiations — where reps get stuck, where customers push back, what packaging doesn't hold up in practice — so Product can continue to refine pricing strategy with real deal data. This is an execution and operations role, not a pricing-strategy-design role: you make pricing work in practice, and make sure the people setting strategy have the ground truth to do it well.

Job Responsibilities:

    40% — Deal Desk & Execution

  • Serve as Redox's Deal Desk for bespoke, non-standard enterprise deals, reviewing and approving pricing before it reaches the customer

  • Pull deal context from account executives and Gong call recordings to understand the customer's business need and where negotiation pressure is coming from

  • Structure pricing for each deal across Redox's three commercial levers — platform fee, connection-based pricing, and transaction-based pricing — within the pricing strategy Product has set

  • Advise reps in real time on structuring responses to specific asks — discounts, multi-year terms, minimum commitments, ramp schedules, and most-favored-nation clauses

  • Partner with Sales leadership, Finance, and Legal to translate approved pricing into contract-ready terms

    • 25% — Pricing Operations & Governance

  • Set and enforce discounting guardrails and approval thresholds so pricing stays consistent and margin-protected deal to deal

  • Build and maintain self-serve pricing tools/models for standard scenarios, so Director-level review is reserved for genuinely bespoke deals

  • Own the operational workflow and systems that support deal pricing approvals (CPQ, Salesforce, or equivalent)

  • Maintain documentation of current pricing rules, exceptions, and approval paths so the process is auditable and repeatable

    • 20% — Cross-Functional Collaboration & Insight

  • Partner with Product, who owns pricing and packaging strategy, to translate that strategy into operational guardrails and Deal Desk practice

  • Track pricing and discounting patterns across closed deals and feed findings back to Product to inform how pricing and packaging strategy evolves

  • Represent the voice of Sales and the field in pricing conversations — what's working, what's not, and where the friction is

  • Partner with Finance to ensure deal pricing decisions align with margin and revenue targets

    • 15% — Change Management & Enablement

  • Lead rollout of pricing and packaging changes approved by Product, including field readiness, adoption planning, and escalation governance

  • Partner with Sales Enablement and field leadership to equip go-to-market teams with the tools, guidance, and collateral needed to operate under new pricing and packaging

  • Provide leadership updates on Deal Desk performance, pricing exceptions, and adoption of new pricing models

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 8+ years in deal desk, sales finance, revenue operations, or pricing operations, ideally at a B2B SaaS company with usage-based or hybrid pricing

  • Proven track record structuring and negotiating complex, multi-element enterprise deals in a Deal Desk or sales finance capacity

  • Experience operationalizing pricing or packaging strategy set by others (Product, pricing strategy teams) into guardrails, tools, and repeatable process

  • Comfortable working directly with reps under deal pressure — clear, fast, decisive

  • Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, with a track record of turning deal and pricing data into clear recommendations

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills — able to work closely with Product, Sales, Finance, and Legal, and to represent field realities credibly to strategy owners

  • Healthcare, health tech, or healthcare interoperability experience is a plus, not required

  • Ability to effectively leverage AI tools in day-to-day work

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field (strongly preferred)

Specific Software Platforms/Tools:

  • Salesforce
  • Gong
  • CPQ/quoting tool
  • Google Suite
  • AI tools (e.g. Claude)
About Redox - Take a look here:

What We Do

Healthcare organizations and technology vendors connect to Redox once, then authorize what data they send to and receive from partners through a centralized hub. Redox's cloud-based platform is vendor and standards-agnostic and enables the secure and efficient exchange of healthcare data.
This approach eradicates the need for point-to-point integrations and accelerates the discovery, adoption, and distribution of patient and provider-facing technology solutions. With hundreds of healthcare organizations and technology vendors exchanging data today, Redox represents the largest interoperable network in healthcare. Learn how you can leverage the Redox platform at .

Other Stuff About Us

Redox is an EEO company. We fully support the diversity of our team. As part of our ongoing work to build more diverse teams at Redox, you will be asked to complete a voluntary EEO survey when applying. This survey is anonymous, we cannot link your application record with your survey responses. We request that you complete this voluntary survey as we run monthly reports for each team which provides data for diversity in terms of gender and ethnic background in our Applicants and our Hired Redoxers. We take this data very seriously and appreciate your willingness and time to complete this step in the process.
Successful candidates must be eligible to be employed in the U.S. and must reside & work in the continental U.S.
Thank you for your interest in Redox!

jobs.description:
Design Assurance Engineer responsible for undertaking National Grid BP141 design assurance roles on a variety of National Grid projects. This role ensures that designs for a variety of installations, asset replacements, connection schemes and substation builds comply with National Grid technical specifications, engineering standards, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.

The successful candidate will work closely with National Grid Project Teams, DNO’s & Contractors, to support the timely delivery of safe, reliable, and compliant designs.

Experience of the UK Electricity Transmission and/or Distribution System is essential for this role.

We are looking for all Design Assurance Disciplines;

  • HV Plant
  • Substation Civil
  • Protection & Control
  • Relay Settings
  • HV Cable
  • Overhead Lines
  • Commissioning Officer

Responsibilities

Design Review & Design Compliance Assurance Audit Report (DCAAR) acceptance:

  • Review and assess design submissions, ensuring compliance with National Grid, technical specifications, procedures and engineering standards.
  • Provide detailed feedback and recommendations to address design gaps, non-compliance, or potential risks.
  • Support completion of design pack DCAAR once all technical, safety, and regulatory requirements are met.
  • Engage in regular project design review meetings with a variety of stakeholders.
  • Coordination and technical interface with other design assurance engineering disciplines.

Stakeholder Coordination:

  • Serve as the primary point of contact between National Grid’s Project Team and Contractor Design Teams regarding design matters.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders, including asset management, project delivery teams, and other engineering disciplines, to ensure design alignment with project objectives.
  • Participate in design coordination meetings, workshops, and technical reviews with contractors and suppliers.

Risk Identification & Mitigation:

  • Identify potential risks related to safety, reliability, and performance in contractor designs and recommend corrective actions.
  • Ensure that Contractor Design Teams have incorporated appropriate risk mitigation measures.
  • Experience of implementing safety by design and CDM awareness.

Documentation & Reporting:

  • Maintain comprehensive records of design submissions, review comments and DCAAR acceptances in accordance with BP188.
  • Review technical reports and assurance documentation related to design pack submission.
  • Monitor performance related to design quality and compliance, providing feedback to management as needed.
  • Experience of working to a structured project design process and compliance with associated BP188 timescales to support the project.

Essential:

  • HNC or Degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, or a related discipline.
  • Currently or previously held National Grid BP141 Design Assurance Engineer authorisation
  • Chartered Engineer status or working towards CEng accreditation
  • Proven experience in infrastructure design, design assurance, or technical approval within the Electricity Transmission and/or DNO sector.
  • Strong knowledge of electrical infrastructure, relevant to the specific assurance discipline.

Desirable:

  • Experience of producing, reviewing and approving designs for National Grid and/or Distribution Network Operator (DNO) projects.
  • Currently or previously nominated as SR188 Contractor Design Approval Engineer on National Grid projects.

Location:

Home based, with the option of working from Omnia offices (Stafford, Stockton Heath and Northallerton), as per project requirements. Must be willing to travel anywhere throughout the UK.

Working Hours:

Ideally full time but willing to consider part time staff positions.

Package:

  • Competitive Salary, plus discretionary bonus
  • Working hours of 40hours per week. All overtime payable or time off in lieu (your choice) should you work more than this
  • 22days holiday, plus bank holidays with an option to increase
  • Private Medical Insurance
  • Workplace Pension
  • Death in Service
  • Company car scheme

Equality, Diversity and Inclusion

We at EGIS are an Equal Opportunities employer and we recognise the value of a Diverse Organisation. EGIS appreciates all job applications. If you decide to apply for an opportunity at EGIS, your application will be assessed based purely on your experience, the essential and desirable criteria, and your suitability for the role. We value each and everyone’s contribution as this builds our culture and means, if you work for EGIS, you will be included, listened to, and respected.

Established in 2012, Omnia Projects is a respected specialist in T&D engineering, project management and technical assurance. With over 110 staff the company has delivered critical infrastructure for clients including National Grid, helping to shape the UK’s evolving energy system.

Omnia Projects brings deep expertise across the full energy project lifecycle, from feasibility and concept design through to commissioning and operation, helping clients navigate the growing complexity of the UK’s energy landscape. The addition of Omnia Projects strengthens Egis’ strategy to deliver a fully integrated service offering in the sector. It enhances capabilities in civil and structural engineering, protection and control and project delivery services for high-voltage substations and overhead line and cable design, creating a broader service offering for clients involved in energy transition and grid modernisation.

Reference Data is part of the Data Enablement team at Addepar. Our mission is to build a scalable, efficient, and high quality data platform that integrates, connects, productionizes, and distributes third-party data content across Addepar and to our clients and partners.

Our goal is to connect data to consumers, creating more value for our downstream clients and services, enabling data to be a language on how the Addepar ecosystem collaborates.

Our Values

jobs.excerpt: Company DescriptionWorkleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006.
jobs.description:
Company Description

Workleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006. We're builders at heart, we make simple products that actually matter to the people who use them. We have two product lines: Workleap Agent, our newest solution built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate, the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here.

Your role

You own the back half of our revenue engine — everything that happens after a deal closes and before cash hits the bank. Every subscription, renewal, and amendment ends up in your team's queue. Your job: make sure each one lands correctly — priced right, invoiced right, recognized right, collected on time.

You'll report to the Director, Finance and lead a small, high-performing team of three who run the day-to-day. The role is deliberately broad: revenue accounting, billing operations, and revenue systems sit together so one person can solve a problem end-to-end.

Your impact:

  • Guarantee the integrity of every dollar of subscription revenue by owning month-end close — revenue journals, deferred revenue schedule, reconciliations, and variance analysis — so Finance has clean numbers before every FP&A review;
  • Keep the systems behind billing running by acting as functional owner of the revenue layer in NetSuite (Advanced Revenue Management) — reliability, data integrity, and continuous improvement are yours;
  • Drive DSO down and reduce manual exceptions every quarter by diagnosing and fixing problems at the source — at the CRM-to-ERP handoff — rather than patching downstream;
  • Run the order-to-invoice cycle across multiple billing entities with accuracy, timeliness, and indirect tax compliance (Avalara, Canadian filings);
  • Deploy AI into team workflows to automate repetitive tasks, surface anomalies faster, and free up bandwidth for higher-value work;
  • Execute structural projects led by Finance leadership — US-entity tax initiative, revenue tech stack review — as the central coordination point across Finance, RevOps, and Customer Success.

Your team

You'll sit inside Finance alongside the Expenses team, with standing relationships across Revenue Operations and Customer Success. You'll manage three direct reports: two Billing & Cash Application Specialists and an Accounts Receivable Analyst who also owns collections. The team is solid — they don't need micromanaging, but they do need a manager who can make the tough calls and unblock the upstream issues that keep eating their time.

The NetSuite implementation and subscription billing migration are behind you. The work ahead is squeezing more out of the stack: fewer manual exceptions every quarter, a tighter CRM-to-ERP handoff, less time between deal close and invoice, more automation in collections. And under Finance leadership, two structural projects are waiting: a tax-optimization initiative to migrate clients to the US entity, and a full review of the revenue tech stack (payment processor, subscription billing, tax engine, and their NetSuite integrations) — with you and your team central to execution.

What you'll bring

  • 7–10 years of finance experience including at least 3 in a revenue accounting, billing operations, or finance operations role inside a SaaS or subscription business;
  • Strong working knowledge of subscription revenue mechanics — recurring billing, contract amendments, renewals, deferred revenue, and how ARR maps to recognized revenue;
  • Solid grasp of ASPE (Section 3400), IFRS 15 or ASC 606 revenue recognition in a subscription context;
  • Hands-on experience with NetSuite (preferred, ideally including Advanced Revenue Management) or an equivalent ERP, plus a subscription billing platform (Recurly, Zuora, Maxio, or similar);
  • Indirect/sales tax experience in a SaaS context — invoice application and return filing; experience with Avalara is an asset;
  • Direct people-leadership experience — you've managed a team, set priorities, and developed your reports;
  • Active, habitual use of AI tools in a finance or operations context — you look for ways to integrate them, not just adapt to them.
  • CPA designation is an asset.

Most of this sounds like you? Apply.

What the job comes with

  • Base salary: $130 to $160k. This range reflects our Canada-wide compensation scale. Final offers may be adjusted based on the candidate's region to align with local market conditions.
  • Annual bonus program.
  • LTIP program, share in Workleap's long-term growth.
  • RRSP + Family health insurance + telemedicine + annual wellness budget.
  • Flexible vacation policy.
  • Remote work, with access to our Montreal office.
  • In-person gathering twice a year.
  • Claude access, for everyone.

Please note: this position is posted under the title Manager, Revenue & Order to Cash, but carries the official title of Manager, Revenue Accounting & Billing within the organization.

What drives us

At Workleap, we build software that sits at the center of how people experience work, every day, at every level.

We move fast. Priorities shift, decisions get made with the information we have, and we iterate. If you thrive on intensity and ambiguity doesn't slow you down, you'll feel right at home.
We're builders. We do what it takes to move forward. AI is part of our toolkit. We use it to go faster and decide smarter, not to replace judgment.

If you want real impact and a place where your decisions matter, this is it.

How we hire

Transparency is how we hire — for you as much as for us.

Here's how it works: a first call with a recruiter, then a virtual interview with the hiring manager. You'll then complete a take-home case study, followed by a meet with future colleagues to discuss it together. Depending on the role, the process may vary slightly — your recruiter will walk you through it on your first call.

We use AI to support certain steps of the process, but every hiring decision remains human.

We can't wait to meet you.

By applying, you confirm that you have read and agree to our privacy policy.

We are a consumer products company selling through major online marketplaces and national retailers. Our business operates across multiple e-commerce platforms, internal systems, and logistics partners, requiring strong coordination, data accuracy, and operational follow-through.
We are seeking a true remote team member who can operate as an extension of our internal marketplace operations team.
Role Overview
This role supports the day-to-day operations of our e-commerce marketplace ecosystem, ensuring product data accuracy, campaign execution, order flow, and internal follow-ups across systems.
This is not a customer-facing role, but it is internally front-facing. The ideal candidate is proactive, analytical, detail-oriented, and comfortable communicating across cross-functional teams to identify issues, follow through, and drive resolution.
The role reports directly to the Marketplace Operations Lead and is expected to grow in responsibility over time.

Key Responsibilities

  • Marketplace & Product Operations
  • Manage and maintain product item creation using Excel-based data feeds
  • Upload, update, and troubleshoot product data attributes across marketplace platforms
  • Monitor and resolve rejected listings, feed errors, and taxonomy changes
  • Perform routine product scrubs to ensure data accuracy and system alignment
  • Campaign & Sponsored Product Support
  • Support setup and monitoring of sponsored product and brand campaigns
  • Pull reporting data from campaign platforms and summarize results
  • Track budgets and ensure campaigns are properly configured and running
  • Order Flow & Issue Resolution
  • Monitor order flow to ensure orders move correctly from marketplace to warehouse
  • Identify stalled, delayed, or unshipped orders
  • Proactively follow up with internal teams to resolve fulfillment issues
  • Ensure resolution is confirmed, not just initiated
  • Internal Communication & Follow-Through
  • Coordinate daily with logistics, operations, and internal teams
  • Follow up persistently on unresolved issues until completion
  • Escalate risks that may impact retailer scorecards or performance metrics
  • Maintain operational momentum and accountability

Reporting & Data Support

  • Pull reports using Excel (including pivot tables where needed)
  • Maintain operational trackers and performance summaries
  • Support leadership with clean, accurate data visibility
  • Systems & Tools
  • Excel (required – strong fundamentals, comfort with reports and pivots)
  • Marketplace feed platforms (training provided)
  • Retailer portals and internal systems (training provided)
  • Canva (nice to have, not required)
  • Prior experience with specific platforms is not required. Training and documentation will be provided. Comfort working in data-heavy environments is essential.

Required Skills & Experience

  • Strong operational and analytical mindset
  • Solid Excel fundamentals (filters, formulas, basic pivots)
  • High attention to detail and data accuracy
  • Comfortable navigating multiple systems simultaneously
  • Confident internal communicator (email, follow-ups, coordination)
  • Proactive problem-solver who does not wait to be told what to fix
  • Strong follow-through until resolution is confirmed

Preferred Profile

  • Experience in e-commerce, marketplaces, or operations support
  • Comfortable working with data feeds, SKUs, UPCs, and inventory logic
  • Experience supporting cross-functional teams (logistics, ops, sales support)
  • South Africa–based candidates preferred due to communication style and ownership mindset

Work Schedule

  • Full-time: 40 hours/week
  • Core preference: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM Eastern Time
  • Open to slight shifts (e.g., 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM ET) if beneficial for operations
  • Compensation & Engagement
  • Full-time, long-term role
  • Initial onboarding and training period expected (90 days)
  • Growth path into deeper ownership of marketplace operations

jobs.title: AVP, Complex Claim Liability Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Who Are We? Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other.
jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That’s the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Job Category

Claim

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$132,800.00 - $219,100.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Investigate, evaluate, reserve, negotiate and resolve the company's most severe and/or complex claims, in multiple jurisdictions, in accordance with Best Practices. Provide quality claim handling and superior customer service on assigned claims, while engaging in indemnity & expense management. Promptly manage claims by completing essential functions including contacts, investigation, damages development, evaluation, reserving, litigation management, negotiating and resolution. Provides consulting and training and serves as an expert technical resource to other claim professionals, business partners, customers, and other stakeholders as appropriate or required. This may include a specific assignment as a severity management resource to one or more field offices.

What Will You Do?

  • CLAIM HANDLING:
  • Directly handle the Company's most severe and complex claims when Travelers has coverage of $2 million or greater and file exposure is greater than $2 million.
  • Provide quality customer service and ensure file quality timely coverage analysis and communication with insured based on application of policy information to facts or allegations of each case.
  • Directly investigate each claim through prompt and strategically-appropriate contact with appropriate parties such as policyholders, accounts, claimants, law enforcement agencies, witnesses, agents, medical providers and technical experts to determine the extent of liability, damages, and contribution potential.
  • Interview witnesses and stakeholders; take necessary statements, as strategically appropriate.
  • Complete outside investigation as needed per case specifics.
  • Actively engage in the identification, selection and direction of appropriate internal and./or external resources for specific activities required to effectively evaluate claims, such as Subro, Risk Control, nurse consultants and fire or fraud investigators and other experts.
  • Verify the nature and extent of injury or property damage by obtaining and reviewing appropriate records and damages documentation.
  • Utilize diary management system to ensure that all claims are handled timely.
  • At required time intervals, evaluate liability & damages exposure.
  • Establish and maintain proper indemnity & expense reserves.
  • Share experience and deep knowledge of creative resolution techniques to improve the claim results of others.
  • Apply the Company's claim quality management protocols, Best Practices and metrics to all claims; document the rationale for any departure from applicable protocols and metrics.
  • Develop and employ creative resolution strategies.
  • Effectively and efficiently manage both allocated and unallocated loss adjustment expenses
  • Evaluate all claims for recovery potential; directly handle recovery efforts and/or engage and direct Company resources for recovery efforts.
  • Responsible for prompt and proper disposition of all claims within delegated authority. Negotiate disposition of claims with insureds and claimants or their legal representatives.
  • Ensure that the right resources are being applied to each claim to achieve the best result at the most optimal cost.
  • LEADERSHIP:
  • Actively provide mentoring and coaching to less experienced claim professionals to increase the technical expertise and improve bench strength.
  • Field Severity Support: Some Complex Claim Specialists may be responsible for all or some of the following:
  • Collaborate with field severity units in the management and evaluation of some of the Company's severe and complex liability claims by providing claim handling guidance, recommendations and strategies to Field Product Line Managers, Unit Managers, and Major Case Specialists, for timely, cost effective resolution of liability major cases.
  • Provide mentoring or training as request by field severity management.
  • COMMUNICATION/INFLUENCE:
  • Consult with Manager on use of Claim Coverage Counsel as needed.
  • Provide guidance to underwriting business partners with res accuracy and adequacy of, and potential future changes to, loss reserves on assigned claims.
  • Recommend appropriate cases for discussion at roundtable.
  • Attend and or present at roundtables/authority discussions for collaboration of technical expertise resulting in improved payout on indemnity and expense.
  • Update appropriate parties as needed, providing new facts as they become available, and their impact upon the liability analysis and settlement options.
  • Represent the company as a technical resource, attend legal proceedings as needed, act within established professional guidelines as well as applicable state laws
  • Obtain and evaluate current information regarding trends in the law; digest and communicate this information to other Company departments and divisions to assist in underwriting and management decisions.
  • Assist underwriting business partners in marketing and account-contact.
  • Actively participate in the coverage, liability and damages analysis and development of creative resolution strategy for severity cases handled in the field.
  • Assist in the recognition of available defenses to contain loss payout and setting of appropriate reserves.
  • Regularly and actively participate in field severity roundtables to share expertise and recommendations in all aspects of severe claim management.
  • Collaborate with the severity unit in compliance with company claim policies, procedures, practices and standards for the handling of cases that meet the Critical Claim referral guidelines.
  • OTHER ACCOUNTABILITIES:
  • Apply expert litigation management through the selection of counsel, evaluation and direction of claim and litigation strategy.
  • Recognize and implement alternate means of resolution.
  • Manages litigated claims. Develop litigation plan with staff or panel counsel, including discovery and legal expenses, to assure effective resolution and to satisfy our customers.
  • Track and control legal expenses to assure cost-effective resolution.
  • Develop and employ innovative techniques to manage expense and outcome when independent counsel is engaged.
  • Attend depositions, mediations, arbitrations, pre-trials, trials and all other legal proceedings, as needed.
  • Closely monitor independent counsel to ensure quality product.
  • Actively participate in periodic file quality reviews.
  • Appropriately deal with information that is considered personal and confidential.
  • Fulfill specific service commitments made to certain accounts, as outlined in Special Account Communication (SAC) instructions, and inquiries from agents and brokers.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • College degree preferred or equivalent business experience.
  • 5-10 years experience handling serious injury and complex liability claims preferred (casualty claim operations environment determining coverage, liability, investigation, research, evaluation, negotiation and settlement).
  • Position requires a proficiency in oral and written communications.
  • Advanced communications skills are required to understand, interpret and convey highly technical information in simple terms to others.
  • Thorough understanding of product lines, objectives of claim management, and legal theory issues involving claim resolution.
  • Familiarity with commercial lines/personal lines products, policy language, exclusions, ISO forms, effective claims handling practices.
  • Extensive experience handling large exposure and/or complex liability claims.
  • Familiarity with commercial lines products, policy language, exclusions, ISO forms, effective claims handling practices.
  • Thorough understanding of the litigation process, relevant case and statutory law.
  • Ability to recognize, analyze and advise on complex coverage, liability and damage issues.
  • Expert written and verbal communication skills to understand, synthesize, interpret and convey complex data.
  • Create and manage positive working relationships with business and marketing partners.
  • Ability to analyze and effectively respond to human resource issues.
  • Utilize technology as a strategic tool.
  • Ability to make independent decisions up to $1,000,000 without involvement of supervisor.
  • Competencies:
  • Leading the Business - Drive Results.
  • Leads Change - Executes Business Strategy.
  • Leading Others - Attract Top Talent, Maximize Individual Performance, Holds Others Accountable, Aligns Rewards, Creates and Sustains a Dynamic Workplace.
  • Leading Self-Emotional Intelligence - Demonstrates Self-Awareness, Initiative and accountability, Applies Critical Thinking, Communications Effectively & Influences Others, Exhibits Courage, Conviction & Credibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Degree or GED.
  • 5 years bodily injury litigation claim handling experience or 10 years litigation experience.
  • In order to perform the essential job functions of this job, acquisition and maintenance of Insurance License(s) may be required to comply with state and Travelers requirements.
  • Generally, license(s) are required to be obtained within three months of starting the job.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members – including spouses, domestic partners, and children – are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit .
